key_insight: The study introduces UPEBNL, a scalable causal Bayesian network framework that makes cancer prescreening models more interpretable while handling large EHR datasets efficiently.
clinical_relevance: It may help clinicians and researchers trace plausible risk pathways from electronic health records for earlier, more transparent prescreening of esophageal and colorectal cancer.
method: Adaptive data slicing to parallelize causal Bayesian network learning
Quality-aware structure aggregation to stabilize learned dependencies
Global DAG construction to produce an interpretable causal graph
evidence_signal: In simulations, UPEBNL improved structural recovery by nearly 40% and reached up to a 221.28-fold speedup; in EHR prescreening it achieved AUCs of 0.8171 for esophageal cancer and 0.784 for colorectal cancer.
watch_item: The causal directions are derived from observational EHR data, so the learned network should be interpreted as putative rather than proven clinical causality.
paper_title: Scalable Causal-Interpretable Machine Learning for Cancer Prescreening Using Electronic Health Records
